title: Knotted Smoky Sichuan Fish Buddha Jumps Over Wall
description: A pescatarian-friendly Sichuan dish featuring almond paste and binchotan-charcoal, perfect for a sick day, with a crumbly and fresh texture, inspired by the traditional Buddha Jumps Over the Wall recipe.
instructions: Start by preparing the smoking mixture by grinding the binchotan charcoal into a fine powder using a spice grinder.
Mix the almond paste with the ground binchotan charcoal, Sichuan peppercorns, and a pinch of salt.
Form the fish balls into knots and set them aside on a plate.
Heat the sesame oil in a wok over medium heat and add the sliced ginger, cooking until fragrant.
Add the chopped scallions and cook for an additional minute, stirring constantly.
Add the soy sauce and stir to combine, cooking for 1 minute.
Add the knotted fish balls to the wok and stir to coat with the sauce.
Cover the wok with a lid and steam the fish balls for 5 minutes, or until cooked through.
Serve the Knotted Smoky Sichuan Fish Buddha Jumps Over Wall hot, garnished with additional scallions and a dollop of the almond paste mixture.
